scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-AI-AGENT-NEEDED.statement: Dispute surge is due to response-speed limitations; an AI agent that auto-answers tickets will resolve the issue.

H-AMI-READ-ERROR.statement: Incorrect or missing AMI register reads from the MDMS are generating erroneous bills that drive disputes.

H-MANUAL-READ-ISSUE.statement: Field manual read processes are failing (missed reads, route execution problems), leading to estimation substitution and disputed bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A recent change to billing import validation rules is causing legitimate reads to be rejected or mis‑applied, producing incorrect bills and disputes.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows more disputed bills associated with actual reads (1785) than estimated reads (1240), indicating that the dispute surge is not driven primarily by estimation substitution.
The tariff change log shows no tariff changes, indicating that tariff alterations are not contributing to the dispute surge.

The observation shows field route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the target of 0.95, indicating that manual read routes are not being completed as planned, which could contribute to estimation substitution and disputed bills.
Dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days < SLA 3.0) despite a high ticket volume of 2440, indicating the surge is not driven by slow response speed.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder asserts there has been no tariff change this year, which matches the tariff change log showing zero changes, indicating tariff alterations are not a driver of the dispute surge.
The observation shows dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 per month in June‑July to ~1,180 in August and 1,260 in September, confirming a surge that began in August.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field stakeholder reports a shortage of three meter readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers, indicating that staffing gaps may drive estimation substitution and contribute to the dispute surge.

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills

framing_assertion.rationale: Customer Service states dispute tickets doubled since August and requests an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and fix the cause.

hypotheses.statement: Dispute surge is due to response-speed limitations; an AI agent that auto-answers tickets will resolve the issue.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, solution is an AI agent; if false, root cause lies elsewhere and AI agent alone will not reduce disputes.

hypotheses.statement: Incorrect or missing AMI register reads from the MDMS are generating erroneous bills that drive disputes.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, fixing MDMS/AMI data quality is required; an AI agent would not reduce disputes.

hypotheses.statement: Field manual read processes are failing (missed reads, route execution problems), leading to estimation substitution and disputed bills.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, improving field read collection or handoff H-FIELD-BILL is needed; AI agent would not address the root cause.

hypotheses.statement: A recent change to billing import validation rules is causing legitimate reads to be rejected or mis‑applied, producing incorrect bills and disputes.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, correcting the validation rule set in DA-RULES is required; AI agent would not fix the underlying bill errors.

actions.decision_impact_rationale: Informs whether response speed limits drive dispute volume; moderate impact on AI agent decision.
